newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil falls, more supply squeezes premiums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil falls, more supply squeezes premiums.

text.p: NWE gas oil staged a partial recovery after a sharp fall on Thursday, following IPE futures, and physical premiums were under pressure from reports of more material from the U.S. and Mediterranean, traders said.
Nov IPE futures ended down $2 at $223.50 a tonne, having climbed back from lows of 219.50, mainly on short-covering.
Traders reported more buying interest but some sellers were reluctant to agree business at lower prices.
"We think the prices are too low. We want to wait until the prices are better," one seller on the barge market said.

One trader offered a cargo of Algerian at Nov IPE +$24 basis Rotterdam for delivery by the end of October but reported no bids. Elsewhere low sulphur diesel was discussed at Nov IPE +$26/27, little changed. Russian cargoes were bid at Nov IPE -$1/+1.25 and offered at +$2.50.

On barges, heating oil traded at Nov IPE +$11.50 fob ARA, unchanged. Diesel was Nov IPE +$30/32. Traders said diesel was under some pressure from U.S. arbitrage cargoes and three Algerians due to arrive in northern Europe shortly.
